planting.note: Set dormant canes in late winter to early spring in well-drained, slightly acidic soil; this selection fruits on primocanes, so a first-year planting can produce a crop the same season under good growing conditions.

directions: Black Magic, bred by John R. Clark at the University of Arkansas under the selection number APF-77, came from a 2002 hand-pollinated cross of APF-12 and Arapaho, with the seedling chosen in 2003 near Clarksville, Arkansas for its primocane-fruiting habit, excellent plant health, and erect canes similar in growth to Ouachita. Its glossy black, slightly conical fruit is large with excellent flavor and better fruit set and development under high summer heat than many earlier primocane-fruiting selections from the program, though it lacks strong postharvest storage life and was not intended for wholesale fresh shipping, making it better suited to home gardens, local markets, and pick-your-own operations. Grow it on a simple trellis in full sun on fertile, well-drained soil, removing spent floricanes after summer harvest and tipping primocanes in midsummer to shape a productive fall crop. It was later patented (U.S. Plant Patent PP24,249) and commercially released under the trade name Black Magic.
